newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL says Q3 results better than expected.
newsitem.headline: MOL says Q3 results better than expected.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas comapny Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt said on Thursday its January-September results exceeded its expectations.
"These results are ahead of our expectations and demonstrate further improvement in the company's financial performance," General Director Zoltan Mandoki said in a company press release.
MOL has published January-September results on Thursday, saying that its consolidated IAS operating profit was 14.7 billion forints and pre-tax profit was 11.6 billion forints. @
Comparative figures for the same period of 1995 were not available, as "reports based on IAS figures were not published prior to 1996," the company said.
MOL's earnings per share for the first nine months were 118 forints, they said.
A 20-year contract signed with Panrusgaz last week on the delivery of natural gas will improve import prices from MOL's perspective, the company said.
"The contract terms allow for fourth quarter imports to be delivered on more favourable terms than expected," MOL said. @
However, the government's decision to delay energy price increases from October 1, 1996 until January 1, 1997 would have a negative impact on this year's results, MOL said.
"Due to the delay... the company will have significant un-earned revenue which will affect operating profit," MOL said.
"Average import unit price was 2.4 forints per cubic meter higher than the (state-controlled) regulated average sales price in the first nine months of 1996," it added.
MOL imported 5.53 billion cubic meters of natural gas in the first nine months of 1996. @

Despite the regulated gas price, the company's exploration and production division produced a 13.9 billion forints operating profit, "mainly due to the fact that intra-company transfer price of crude oil has increased," MOL said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 1,650 forints, up 30.
